q: Huygens' principle states that every point on a wavefront may be considered as a source of _____ wavelets.
e: In 1678 the Dutch physicist Christiaan Huygens stated the wave theory of light. Every point on a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets of the same frequency and speed. Huygens' wavelets are secondary.

q: The new position of wavefront is the _____ of the wavelets.
e: The new wavefront is the envelope of Huygens' secondary wavelets. The centres of those wavelets sit back on the old front. The new front is the envelope, not the wavelet centres.

q: If the propagating wave is transmitted through the medium at a speed $v$, the secondary wavelets will have the same frequency and _____.
e: propagating and wave have to stay with the same process. A different driver in place of propagating would describe a different law. Pitch is frequency; amplitude is loudness.

q: A wavefront is defined as a surface associated with a propagating wave which is a locus of all points in the wave that have the same _____.
e: Phase angle is angular position on a reference circle, from 0 to 2 pi each cycle. A difference of 0 or 2 pi is in phase; pi is fully out of phase. Pitch is frequency; amplitude is loudness.

q: A wavefront is always _____ to the direction of propagation or rays.
e: Propagation is travel of the wave through the medium. Along the way the wave can bounce, bend or weaken. A wavefront is perpendicular to the rays.

q: There are two types of wavefront; plane wavefront and _____ wavefront.
e: A wavefront is the surface of equal phase. Rays stand perpendicular to it. The two listed types are plane and spherical; far away, spherical becomes plane.

q: The spherical wavefront from a source transforms into _____ wavefront when it is far away from the source.
e: A wavefront is the surface of equal phase. Rays stand perpendicular to it. Far from the source the spherical front becomes plane.

q: The angular position of a point of a periodic wave on a reference circle is known as the _____ angle.
e: Refraction bends a wave when its speed changes from one medium to another. Sound can be reflected, refracted or attenuated as it travels. The angular position on the reference circle is phase angle.

q: If the phase difference between two positions is $0, 2\pi, 4\pi, \dots$, these two positions are _____.
e: Phase difference is how far two waves' phase angles sit apart at the same instant. Delta phi = (2 pi / lambda) Delta x links it to path difference. 0 or 2 pi is in phase; coherence is a source property.

q: If the phase difference is $\pi, 3\pi, 5\pi, \dots$, these two positions are completely _____.
e: Phase difference is how far two waves' phase angles sit apart at the same instant. Delta phi = (2 pi / lambda) Delta x links it to path difference. 0 or 2 pi is in phase; coherence is a source property. Integer wavelengths of path are in phase; odd half-wavelengths are out of phase.

q: Path difference indicates the distance between two points measured along the direction of _____ of the wave.
e: Path difference is extra distance along the propagation direction. It is not a sideways gap. Path difference is measured along propagation, not along the oscillation.

q: If the path difference between two waves is $0, \lambda, 2\lambda, \dots$, it is said to be in _____.
e: Path difference is extra distance along the propagation direction. It is not a sideways gap. Integer wavelengths of path are in phase.

q: If the path difference is $\frac{\lambda}{2}, \frac{3\lambda}{2}, \frac{5\lambda}{2}, \dots$, it is said completely out of _____.
e: Path difference is extra distance along the propagation direction. It is not a sideways gap. The wave language is out of phase.

q: In the relation $\Delta\theta = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x$, $\Delta\theta$ represents the _____ difference.
e: Path difference is extra distance along the travel direction. m lambda is in phase and bright; odd half-wavelengths are out of phase and dark. Delta theta is phase difference; Delta x is path.

q: In the relation $\Delta\theta = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x$, $\lambda$ represents the _____ of the waves.
